channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Zelenskyy Says US Floats NATO Membership in Deal for Donbas
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said US peace envoys asked whether Ukraine would be willing to give up the Donbas region in the nation’s east to Russia in exchange for NATO membership, signaling a potential shift in Washington’s negotiating tactics.
item.dc:creator: Volodymyr Verbianyi

item.title: The Nuclear Investment Boom in Eastern Europe Picks Up Pace
item.description: After Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, Eastern Europe moved to diversify energy from Moscow
item.dc:creator: Jan Bratanic, Daniel Hornak and Jonathan Tirone

item.title: Burnham Tries to Hush Down His Own Talk of Rejoining the EU
item.description: Six weeks ago Andy Burnham suggested Britain “could go all the way” and rejoin the European Union. This week he downplayed his own idea: “No one’s talking about rejoining.”
item.dc:creator: Alex Wickham

item.title: Democrats Ask Musk to Preserve Documents on Starlink in Ukraine
item.description: Democrats on the Senate Foreign Relations Committee have asked SpaceX Chief Executive Officer Elon Musk to “preserve all documents, communications and electronically stored information” related to the company’s Starlink and Starshield systems in Ukraine,” according to a letter released Friday.
item.dc:creator: Dana Hull

item.title: All Airports Are Ground Stopped Until Further Notice: FAA
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Ray LaHood, former US Transportation Secretary, says he believes the nationwide FAA ground stop is more likely the result of an old, antiquated system failing than problems transitioning to new technology. LaHood says travelers should consider alternate plans because disruptions could continue even after the system is restored, and says major airports are prepared to handle the fallout. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump to Hold Trilateral Meeting With Xi, Putin in China
item.description: President Donald Trump will meet China’s Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin Nov. 19 on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, a White House spokeswoman said.
item.dc:creator: Courtney Subramanian and Jeff Mason

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily Podcast: Jensen’s Nvidia Departure
item.description:
The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF
After weeks spent denying the allegations of infidelity and fighting to remain in his job as Nvidia’s chief executive officer, Jensen Huang’s surrender late Wednesday night was unconditional. His usual take-charge demeanor had evaporated, according to a person familiar with the situation, and he’d started using phrases like “whatever” and “I don’t care.” Huang’s admittance to an affair with an alleged spy has had an international ripple effect across the AI and tech industry.
On today’s episode:
Ian King, Bloomberg News US Semiconductors Reporter Cat Barton, Bloomberg News Seoul Bureau Chief Joe Wiesenthal, Bloomberg ‘Odd Lots’ Podcast Co-Host Mark Jacobson, International Spy Museum Historian (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: LaHood Says Antiquated FAA System Likely Failed
item.description: Ray LaHood, former US Transportation Secretary, says he believes the nationwide FAA ground stop is more likely the result of an old, antiquated system failing than problems transitioning to new technology. LaHood says travelers should consider alternate plans because disruptions could continue even after the system is restored, and says major airports are prepared to handle the fallout. He speaks with Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Ground Stop Fix Will 'Take Some Time,' Mullin Says
item.description: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin says it will take some time to resolve issues affecting flights around the country. All flights have been grounded. He can't rule out the reason is a cyber attack, but he says travelers are safe. “It’s going to take some time, and so this isn’t going to just be resolved and turned around within the hour. This is going to take take some time,” he told reporters at the White House on Friday. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Hungary Finds $20 Million Cash in Probe of Orban Minister
item.description: Investigators have found nearly $20 million worth of cash hidden in forests, barns and warehouses across Hungary, a breakthrough in the widening probes into alleged corruption by allies of former Premier Viktor Orban.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Escritt and Andras Gergely

item.title: The Best of the 2026 Bloomberg New Economy Forum
item.description: A recap of the 2026 Bloomberg New Economy Forum, held in New Delhi in October 2026, featuring interviews with global leaders in business and government. Hosted by Erik Schatzker. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Jensen Huang Scandal Fallout Grows
item.description: A Chinese company founded by Alice Huang, the woman at the center of a controversy dogging Nvidia, procured smuggled AI chips that were installed at a Shanghai data center with links to Megaspeed International, according to documents reviewed by Bloomberg News. Bloomberg News Seoul Bureau Chief Cat Barton takes an international view of Jensen Huang’s downfall. Bloomberg News US Semiconductor Reporter Ian King also brings an exclusive inside look at Huang’s final hours as Nvidia CEO. Plus, Bloomberg News Technology Reporter Matt Day has the update and fallout of Microsoft’s massive services outage. Finally, Lis Agosto, Director of Product Research & Strategy at Global X ETFs, takes an investor’s view on the Nvidia scandal. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Administration Lets States Delay New Medicaid Work Rules
item.description: The Trump administration will let states delay a requirement that some people in the Medicaid program work, volunteer or go to school to get health insurance, pausing a controversial policy that would throw millions of people’s health coverage into question.
item.dc:creator: Rachel Cohrs Zhang

item.title: Three Issues Where Congress Could Strike a Deal Next Year
item.description: With the White House sending threatening letters, any compromises will have to come from Capitol Hill.
item.dc:creator: Nathan R Dean

item.title: Deciphering Nvidia Noise, US Retirement Gets C+, Anthropic IPO Ahead
item.description: Bloomberg Money takes the pulse of your financial life, powered by the reporting of our global newsroom. Today's guests: Hartree Partners Senior Advisor & Commodities Strategist Ed Morse and Marsh Global Defined Benefit & Contribution Leader Christine Mahoney. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rubio Labels International Law a Tool of Elites, Attacks ICC
item.description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio delivered an aggressive and unrepentant challenge to international law in a speech on Friday, warning that the US would never submit to the “sterile vision of radical judges or soulless global bureaucrats.”
item.dc:creator: Eric Martin

item.title: What Comes Next For Dems After ‘Blue Wave’
item.description: David Gura and Tom Keene discuss the future of the Democratic Party this week’s edition of “Bloomberg Money.” As Chris Van Hollen challenges Chuck Schumer for the Senate Majority Leader job, Tom and David also discuss their must-read books: “What It Took to Win: A History of the Democratic Party” by Michael Kazin and “Supermajority: How Democrats Can Build Lasting Power” by Adam Jentleson. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Kevin Hassett Says He Will Remain as Trump Economic Adviser
item.description: National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett denied a report that he plans to depart his post in the coming weeks.
item.dc:creator: Saleha Mohsin and Courtney Subramanian

item.title: Richer on Paper, Americans Still Feel Price Pain
item.description: Bloomberg’s Sarah Foster joins Tom Keene on “Bloomberg Money.” By the numbers, Americans have never been richer. The stock market has doubled in four years, the economy keeps growing, unemployment is near historic lows and home values are holding steady. But Tuesday’s election results suggest a different reality for many voters. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Mamdani Strikes Deal With Trump on Bodega Food Stamp Rules
item.description: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said he reached a deal with President Donald Trump that will give small retailers nationwide, including about 10,000 city bodegas, more time to comply with new federal food stamp requirements.
item.dc:creator: Cameron Fozi and Laura Nahmias
